consensus_view: The expectation baseline is not yet documented in the candidate registry.
economic_mechanism: Sustained AI memory demand can improve mix, utilization, customer allocation, and forward revenue visibility.
expected_validation_event: Next official peer filing or reviewed analyst-revision evidence.
red_team_objection: Micron evidence alone may describe company-specific execution rather than a non-consensus memory-wide demand inflection.
summary: Reviewed Micron SEC evidence supports a bounded candidate that AI-linked memory demand remains strong. The candidate still needs an explicit expectation baseline before it can be framed as stronger than consensus.
theme_name: AI-linked memory demand remains strong, but expectation baseline still needed
variant_view: Micron official evidence indicates durable AI-linked memory demand, but the non-consensus element is not proven until expectations and peer evidence are added.
what_would_confirm: Peer filings or official IR evidence confirm similar AI-linked memory demand, with analyst revisions aligning to the fundamental improvement.
what_would_falsify: Demand proves pulled forward, customer commitments weaken, inventory rises, or peers fail to confirm the same pattern.

consensus_view: Memory remains cyclical unless contract terms and customer behavior prove otherwise.
economic_mechanism: Commitments can improve revenue visibility, allocation discipline, and pricing bands, but only if volumes and terms remain enforceable.
expected_validation_event: Future Micron filings and peer filings showing whether commitment structures persist.
red_team_objection: Customer commitments can improve Micron visibility without changing the memory industry's core cyclicality.
summary: Reviewed Micron SEC evidence supports a company-specific candidate that customer commitments may improve revenue durability. It does not prove the memory industry has structurally lower cyclicality.
theme_name: Customer commitments may improve Micron revenue durability, but industry cyclicality reduction is unproven
variant_view: Micron's customer-commitment disclosures may reduce near-term revenue volatility for Micron, while broader industry cyclicality remains unproven.
what_would_confirm: Official evidence shows durable RPO conversion, enforceable minimums, pricing protection, or peer adoption of similar commitment structures.
what_would_falsify: Commitments prove cancellable, low-margin, concentrated, short duration, or fail to protect revenue in a weaker demand window.

consensus_view: NAND and enterprise SSD recovery needs proof beyond one issuer's product and revenue disclosures.
economic_mechanism: Improving enterprise SSD demand can lift NAND mix, absorb supply, support pricing, and improve storage-segment margins if confirmed.
expected_validation_event: Peer filings, NAND pricing updates, and reviewed inventory or margin evidence.
red_team_objection: Micron product milestones and company commentary may not prove a broad NAND or enterprise SSD cycle acceleration.
summary: Reviewed Micron SEC evidence supports a bounded candidate that Micron's NAND and enterprise SSD indicators may be improving. A broader cycle call still needs peer, pricing, inventory, and margin confirmation.
theme_name: NAND and enterprise SSD may be improving, but peer and pricing confirmation is missing
variant_view: Micron's reviewed evidence may be an early sign of improving AI storage and NAND demand, but broad acceleration is not yet proven.
what_would_confirm: WDC, SNDK, Kioxia, or other official sources show improving enterprise SSD/NAND demand with pricing, inventory, or margin support.
what_would_falsify: NAND pricing weakens, inventories rebuild, peers fail to confirm, or improvement is isolated to Micron product timing.

consensus_view: Capex may be needed to support constrained high-value AI memory demand.
economic_mechanism: New capacity can shift scarcity into balanced supply or oversupply if demand growth slows, mix changes, or peer additions arrive together.
expected_validation_event: Future capex disclosures from Micron and memory peers.
red_team_objection: Elevated capex can be a rational response to constrained AI demand rather than evidence of overbuild.
summary: Reviewed Micron SEC evidence supports a medium-term red-flag candidate that elevated capex could create supply catch-up risk. The candidate is not a cycle-top call because capex mix and demand backing still matter.
theme_name: Micron capex creates medium-term supply catch-up risk, but capex mix matters
variant_view: If capex broadens into commodity capacity or peers also accelerate supply, it could become a medium-term supply catch-up risk.
what_would_confirm: Official evidence shows broad commodity capacity expansion, peer capex acceleration, utilization risk, or inventory rebuild.
what_would_falsify: Capex is concentrated in HBM, node migration, packaging, or demand-backed capacity with continued supply discipline.

consensus_view: A single US close-to-close reaction can be noise unless peers, regions, and revisions confirm it.
economic_mechanism: A rewarded event can validate fundamental evidence when direct issuer reaction and peer reaction outperform the benchmark, but persistence and regional confirmation are required.
expected_validation_event: Next Asia close-to-close confirmation, analyst revisions, and 48-hour price persistence review.
red_team_objection: The evidence proves only a reviewed US close-to-close reaction; it does not eliminate sell-the-news risk or prove global memory-chain confirmation.
summary: Reviewed US market reaction evidence supports a first-pass candidate that Micron's earnings were rewarded in the US close-to-close window. The candidate remains capped because Asia confirmation, analyst revisions, and 48-hour persistence evidence are still missing.
theme_name: US market rewarded Micron earnings, but Asia and analyst confirmation are missing
variant_view: Reviewed MU, WDC, SNDK, STX, and QQQ evidence supports a US confirming reaction, but not a global memory-chain confirmation.
what_would_confirm: SK Hynix, Samsung, Kioxia, or 7709.HK confirm the reaction; analyst revisions improve; and MU/storage peers avoid a quick fade.
what_would_falsify: MU or storage peers reverse materially while QQQ remains firm, Asia memory names fail to confirm, or analyst revisions focus on capex and supply risk.

consensus_view: Broadcom is already widely associated with AI semiconductors, so the baseline likely expects AI contribution; the precise RPO conversion and margin impact are not yet reviewed.
economic_mechanism: Longer-duration custom accelerator commitments can improve revenue visibility, networking attach, and investment planning, but only if margins and customer concentration are acceptable.
expected_validation_event: Manual review of AVGO 10-Q sections and next Broadcom official earnings or filing update.
red_team_objection: The candidate may be consensus AI beta dressed as alpha unless contract durability and margin conversion are proven.
summary: Broadcom's locally extracted 10-Q includes AI data center, custom AI accelerator, AI networking, and large remaining performance obligation references. Because the evidence is still draft, this is only a Watch candidate.
theme_name: Broadcom custom AI accelerator demand visibility may be improving, but conversion and concentration need review
variant_view: The official 10-Q metadata and extraction suggest custom AI accelerator commitments may provide revenue visibility beyond generic AI beta exposure.
what_would_confirm: Reviewed AVGO filing sections show durable custom AI accelerator obligations, healthy margin conversion, and demand visibility that is not only boilerplate.
what_would_falsify: The obligation language proves one-off, low margin, highly concentrated, cancellable, or already fully reflected in consensus expectations.

consensus_view: Oracle cloud growth is known, but the cost and bottleneck economics of AI infrastructure build-out need source-level review.
economic_mechanism: Physical AI infrastructure constraints can raise supplier terms, energy costs, capex commitments, and execution risk while also indicating strong demand if revenue conversion is proven.
expected_validation_event: Manual review of ORCL 10-K capex/risk/MD&A sections and peer hyperscaler filings.
red_team_objection: This may be generic cloud risk-factor language rather than a differentiated alpha candidate until exact filing sections are reviewed.
summary: Oracle's locally extracted 10-K contains dense cloud, data center, AI infrastructure, power, GPU, memory-device, capex, pricing, and margin references. This supports a Watch candidate around AI infrastructure bottlenecks, not a reviewed signal.
theme_name: Oracle OCI AI infrastructure bottleneck risk may be rising, but direct capex economics need review
variant_view: OCI demand may be constrained or made more expensive by power, data center sites, networking hardware, server availability, GPUs, and memory devices.
what_would_confirm: Reviewed ORCL filing language confirms material power, data center, GPU, memory, or networking constraints tied to OCI growth and capex economics.
what_would_falsify: The extracted references are boilerplate, constraints are immaterial, or revenue conversion offsets the cost and commitment risks.

consensus_view: The common market framing emphasizes GPU scarcity and broad AI capex, while non-GPU component bottlenecks need harder evidence.
economic_mechanism: If non-GPU components become scarce, pricing power and allocation may shift toward component suppliers while cloud builders face higher capex, less favorable terms, or delayed revenue conversion.
expected_validation_event: Manual review of ORCL and AVGO filings, then peer supplier filings and pricing or lead-time evidence.
red_team_objection: This candidate could be too broad unless follow-up evidence isolates which component, supplier, and economic mechanism matter.
review_notes: Umbrella Watch candidate. Split into narrower tracks for evidence collection.
summary: Local ORCL 10-K and AVGO 10-Q extractions both reference AI infrastructure build-out and component or supplier constraints. This supports a Watch candidate that bottlenecks may extend beyond headline GPUs into memory, networking, and other critical components.
theme_name: AI infrastructure component scarcity may extend beyond GPUs, but supplier confirmation is missing
variant_view: Cross-company SEC evidence may indicate broader AI infrastructure scarcity across power, memory devices, networking, server availability, custom accelerators, and supplier terms.
what_would_confirm: Reviewed filings from cloud buyers and component suppliers show recurring non-GPU constraints, pricing pressure, allocation, or extended lead times.
what_would_falsify: The references are boilerplate, constraints are transitory, pricing does not move, or suppliers report normal lead times and inventory.

consensus_view: Broadcom is already treated as an AI semiconductor beneficiary, so generic AI exposure is not alpha.
economic_mechanism: Durable custom accelerator commitments can convert into revenue visibility; networking attach can expand wallet share; margin conversion determines whether demand becomes economic value.
expected_validation_event: Manual review of AVGO 10-Q RPO, custom AI accelerator, AI networking, customer concentration, and margin sections.
red_team_objection: This could still be consensus AVGO AI beta unless contract durability and margin economics are proven by reviewed source passages.
review_notes: Narrower than umbrella candidate TC-AI-INFRA-COMPONENT-SCARCITY-20260627 because it isolates AVGO custom AI accelerator and AI networking demand visibility instead of broad component scarcity.
summary: Narrow track split from the broad component-scarcity umbrella. AVGO 10-Q extraction points to custom AI accelerators, AI racks, AI networking products, RPO, customer concentration, and margin conversion. This is narrower because it tests one supplier and two adjacent product layers: custom accelerators and AI networking.
theme_name: AVGO custom AI accelerator and AI networking demand visibility needs contract and margin review
variant_view: Contracted custom AI accelerator demand and AI networking attach may provide more durable revenue visibility than generic semiconductor beta if RPO quality, customer concentration, and margins hold up.
what_would_confirm: Reviewed AVGO filing language shows durable non-cancellable custom AI accelerator obligations, AI networking demand, and margin/operating income conversion.
what_would_falsify: The RPO is mostly software or cancellable, the customer exposure is too concentrated, margin conversion is weak, or the text is already-consensus AI beta.

consensus_view: Oracle cloud and AI infrastructure build-out are visible, but the market may treat data center constraints as generic risk disclosure.
economic_mechanism: If OCI demand requires scarce power, sites, servers, GPUs, memory, and networking hardware, Oracle may face higher capex and less favorable supplier terms while component suppliers may gain pricing or allocation power.
expected_validation_event: Manual review of ORCL 10-K OCI, data center, capex, risk factor, contractual obligation, and MD&A sections.
red_team_objection: This has the highest boilerplate risk because much of the scarcity language may be risk-factor disclosure rather than a live bottleneck.
review_notes: Narrower than umbrella candidate TC-AI-INFRA-COMPONENT-SCARCITY-20260627 because it isolates ORCL buyer-side OCI data center power/site/server availability constraints instead of broad component scarcity.
summary: Narrow track split from the broad component-scarcity umbrella. ORCL 10-K extraction points to OCI demand, data center expansion, capex, power/site constraints, networking hardware, server availability, GPUs, memory devices, and supplier commitments. This is narrower because it tests Oracle buyer-side infrastructure constraints rather than broad supplier scarcity.
theme_name: ORCL OCI data center power, site, and server availability bottleneck needs boilerplate review
variant_view: OCI growth may be constrained or made more capital-intensive by power availability, permitted sites, networking hardware, server availability, GPUs, and memory devices.
what_would_confirm: Reviewed ORCL filing language shows material OCI demand and specific power, site, server, GPU, memory, networking, or supplier constraints tied to capex economics or revenue conversion.
what_would_falsify: The language is boilerplate, constraints are immaterial, customer demand fails to convert, or capex economics are adequately offset by revenue growth.
